about.title: Every equation has a sound.
about.desc: How x=arcsin y turns equations into music, and who is behind it.
about.lede: x=arcsin y is a music project. Each track takes one equation and lets it drive the part you remember.
about.html:
Math × Music × Code × AI = Math Sound

How a track gets made

  1. An equation gets picked.A square wave's Fourier series, the digits of π, a chaotic map. It has to be able to do something you can hear.
  2. AI composes the track and writes the code.Melody, chords, drums, form, mix.
  3. The code calculates every sample.No recordings, no sample packs, no human voice. The choirs, accordions and whistles are arithmetic too.
  4. A person listens.Naru Kijima listens and decides what stays. Passing technical checks doesn't count as finished. Being worth hearing does.

What an equation does, and doesn't

An equation doesn't write a whole track. On each track page you'll see what the equation decides and what was composed, side by side. In 1/x it's the falling whistle. In 3.14159 it's how many times the hi-hat strikes in each beat.

The name

The label is y=sin(x), the sine wave that every sound here can be built from. The artist is its inverse, x=arcsin y: going from the sound back to the formula.

Sheet music

The notes of all 35 tracks of f(t) are public under Scores. Press play and the page follows along.

Made with AI

This music is made with AI, and we say so: it's declared to our distributor and labeled on our social posts. x=arcsin y is a project name, not a person. Production credit goes to Naru Kijima.

Using the music

Put a track in your videos and posts. You don't need to ask. Platforms may run ads on those videos automatically, because the albums are registered with their audio matching systems. Remixes and sampling aren't allowed. The details are in the terms.

The code

This site's code is on GitHub, under the MIT license. The music, the scores and the words aren't: those follow the terms.

Questions

Can I use a track in my video?
Yes, without asking, personal or business. Credit is welcome, not required. On TikTok and Instagram, add it from the app's music library.
Why did my video get a copyright claim?
Audio matching found the track. Ads may run on the video, and the earnings may go to the rights holder. If it causes a problem, write to us with the link.
Can I play the scores?
Yes, including on video.
Can I remix it or sample it?
No. The albums are registered with Content ID, which doesn't allow that. The equations are free for anyone, so you can always make your own sound from them.
Can I use it in a game, an app, a film or a paid ad?
Write first.
How do I get in touch?

terms.title: Terms
terms.html:
Updated 2026-11-07

Quick answers

Can I put a track in my YouTube video, Short or social post?
Yes. You don't need to ask, whether the channel is personal or a business.
Will my video get a copyright claim?
It may get an automatic Content ID claim. That's the matching system, not a complaint from us, and it isn't a strike. Ads may run, and the earnings may go to the rights holder. Write to us with the link, and we can release the claim on that video.
Can I use it on TikTok or Instagram?
Yes. Add the track from the app's music library.
Do I have to credit you?
No, but we'd love it. For example: Music: x=arcsin y, "y=sin(x)".
Can I use it in a game, an app, an ad or a film?
Write first. We want the music used. Tell us what you're making and which track, and we'll work out the details, including how to keep videos of your game or app free of claims.
Can I play the scores or cover a track?
Play the scores and post your performance, yes. To release a cover on streaming services, write first.
Can I remix it, sample it or use it in my own song?
No. The distributor doesn't allow it.
Is this royalty-free or Creative Commons?
No. It's free to use in the ways on this page, and the full terms are below.

What you can do without asking

  • Use a whole track in your videos and social posts, personal or business.
  • Listen, read and download the scores, study them, and play them yourself, including on video.
  • Use the equations however you like. They're math, and math belongs to everyone.

Credit is welcome, not required.

What automatic systems may do

The album is registered with platforms' audio matching systems, such as YouTube Content ID, through its distributor. When a video uses a track, ads may run on it and the earnings may go to the rights holder. That's automatic, and it isn't a complaint from us. YouTube may block a Short longer than one minute when it has a claim, so keep Shorts to a minute or less. On TikTok and Instagram, add tracks from the app's music library. If a video of yours has a problem, write to us with the link.

What needs a conversation first

Paid advertising, games, apps, films and anything else that builds a track into a product: write first.

What isn't allowed

  • Remixing a track, sampling it, or using any sound from it in your own music.
  • Uploading a track to a store, a streaming service or a music library, or presenting it as your own.
  • Training AI models on the recordings or the scores.

This isn't an open, Creative Commons or royalty-free license. The original work stays with x=arcsin y, and nothing here transfers it.

What we can't promise

  • This music is made with AI, and everything here is provided as it is.
  • The scores are transcriptions generated from the code that plays the music. They are simplified and may contain errors or differ from what you hear.
  • The site may change or go offline at any time.

Liability

To the extent the law allows, we aren't liable for damages arising from this site or from your use of what's on it. External links, such as streaming services and social platforms, are run by others under their own terms.

Changes

We may update these terms. The date above shows the latest version.

Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of Japan.

Contact

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.desc: What xarcsiny.com does and doesn't collect.
privacy.lede: No accounts, no ads, no cookies.
privacy.html:
Effective 2026-11-01

What we collect

This site has no sign-up form, no ads and no tracking cookies. It asks you for nothing.

Hosting

The site runs on Cloudflare. To deliver pages and keep them secure, Cloudflare processes technical request data such as IP address, browser and the page requested. We also use Cloudflare Web Analytics, which counts visits without cookies. We see all this only as aggregated traffic numbers, such as how many times a page was opened. See Cloudflare's privacy policy.

Stored on your device

Your browser remembers your library view (list or plots) in local storage. This stays on your device and isn't sent to us.

If you email us

We use your address and message only to reply, and don't share them except where the law requires.

Outside links

Links to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, DistroKid, YouTube, TikTok and Instagram lead to services with their own privacy policies.

Changes and contact

We may update this policy. The date above shows the latest version. Questions: {CONTACT}
